name: Recommendations
description: The service suggests titles that feel relevant to the user's interests, viewing history, current mood, and household profile.
aliases: recommendations| suggested titles| personalized rows| content suggestions| recommended for you
examples: The recommendations matched what I usually watch.  The same titles kept appearing in different rows.  I found a new show through a suggestion that suited my mood.

name: Content Discovery
description: The service helps users encounter suitable new, unfamiliar, or relevant content without requiring a precise title in advance.
aliases: content discovery| discover titles| finding something new| browsing content| title discovery
examples: I found something interesting without knowing exactly what I wanted.  Browsing did not lead me to anything suitable.  A category row helped me discover a new series.

name: Profile Personalization
description: Profiles keep viewing history, recommendations, saved content, and preferences appropriately separated and tailored to each user.
aliases: profile personalization| user profile| profile separation| personalized profile| viewing profile
examples: My profile showed recommendations that reflected my tastes.  Another person's viewing affected what appeared for me.  Switching to the correct profile immediately improved the suggestions.

name: Search
description: Search helps users locate specific titles, genres, languages, people, or content types through relevant and understandable results.
aliases: search| title search| genre search| find content| search results
examples: Search found the exact title quickly.  The results were too broad for what I entered.  Searching by genre helped me avoid a long browsing session.

name: Casual Viewing
description: The service supports relaxed, spontaneous viewing when users want entertainment without extensive planning or comparison.
aliases: casual viewing| spontaneous viewing| easy entertainment| unplanned watching| relaxed viewing
examples: I opened Netflix and found something fun almost immediately.  I did not want to compare many options.  The service made an unplanned evening session feel easy.

name: Navigation
description: Users can move through screens, rows, menus, profiles, and playback areas without losing orientation or taking unnecessary steps.
aliases: navigation| wayfinding| menu movement| browsing flow| screen navigation
examples: It was clear how to return to the previous screen.  I had to move through too many rows to reach what I wanted.  The menu structure made the main areas easy to find.

name: Watchlist Management
description: Users can add, remove, review, and locate saved titles in a way that supports planned viewing and later retrieval.
aliases: watchlist| my list| saved titles| list management| saved content
examples: I found a show I had saved earlier.  Adding a title to My List was straightforward.  My saved content was harder to locate than expected.

name: Cross-Device Experience
description: Viewing activity, progress, profiles, and discovery carry across devices in a way that supports smooth transitions between them.
aliases: cross-device experience| device switching| phone to TV| laptop to TV| multi-device viewing
examples: I started on my phone and continued on the TV without trouble.  My progress did not seem current on the second device.  Switching devices fit naturally into my viewing routine.

name: Visual Organization
description: The interface arranges rows, controls, labels, and content information in a structured way that supports scanning and comparison.
aliases: visual organization| interface structure| organized rows| layout clarity| information arrangement
examples: The rows were organized in a way that made comparison easy.  Important controls appeared where I expected them.  The screen structure helped me review several titles efficiently.

name: Playback
description: Starting, pausing, resuming, seeking, and controlling video works predictably and supports uninterrupted viewing.
aliases: playback| video controls| pause and resume| seeking| player controls
examples: The episode resumed from the correct point.  I triggered the controls accidentally.  Pausing and continuing the video worked as expected.

name: Mobile Experience
description: The service works effectively on smartphones and tablets, including touch interaction, small-screen browsing, and mobile playback.
aliases: mobile experience| smartphone use| tablet use| mobile interface| touch interaction
examples: The app was easy to use during a short phone session.  Small controls caused accidental taps.  Browsing on the tablet felt clear and responsive.

name: Quick Viewing
description: The service supports users who want to find and start suitable content with minimal browsing, reading, or setup.
aliases: quick viewing| fast start| minimal browsing| immediate playback| rapid selection
examples: I found something and started watching within a minute.  Too many choices slowed down a simple session.  A familiar row helped me begin quickly.

name: Interrupted Viewing
description: The service supports sessions that are paused, stopped, resumed later, or repeatedly moved in and out of playback.
aliases: interrupted viewing| stop and resume| unfinished titles| viewing interruptions| session continuity
examples: I returned later and continued where I stopped.  After an interruption, it was difficult to recover my place.  The service handled several short viewing sessions well.

name: Accessibility
description: The interface supports users with visual, hearing, motor, or other access needs through perceivable content and usable controls.
aliases: accessibility| accessible interface| assistive needs| inclusive design| access support
examples: The subtitles made the dialogue accessible.  Low-contrast labels were difficult to distinguish.  The controls remained usable despite my visual or motor needs.

name: Family Viewing
description: The service supports shared household sessions, family-friendly selection, and transitions between individual and group viewing contexts.
aliases: family viewing| household viewing| shared viewing| family content| watching together
examples: We found a film suitable for everyone.  Switching between family and individual viewing was easy.  The setup reduced friction during a shared evening session.

name: Content Boundaries
description: The service keeps children's, adult, and profile-specific content contexts appropriately separated within a shared household.
aliases: content boundaries| kids content| adult content| profile boundaries| household separation
examples: Children's content stayed within the children's profile.  Adult recommendations appeared too close to the family context.  The profiles preserved clear boundaries between viewing modes.

name: Visual Readability
description: Text, labels, descriptions, subtitles, and interface states are legible at the user's viewing distance and under relevant display conditions.
aliases: visual readability| text legibility| readable labels| subtitle readability| screen readability
examples: The description was easy to read from the sofa.  Small secondary text required extra effort.  Increasing the subtitle size made viewing comfortable.

name: Visual Browsing
description: Artwork, thumbnails, previews, and visual hierarchy help users scan options and judge what may be worth watching.
aliases: visual browsing| thumbnails| artwork| previews| visual hierarchy
examples: The thumbnails helped me decide quickly.  Similar-looking artwork made the rows hard to scan.  A visually engaging preview drew me to a suitable title.

name: Selective Viewing
description: The service supports users who apply clear standards and want to evaluate a smaller set of high-quality, relevant options.
aliases: selective viewing| careful selection| high standards| curated choice| deliberate selection
examples: I wanted one strong option rather than many generic choices.  I compared several descriptions before deciding.  The service helped narrow the selection to content that met my criteria.

name: Background Viewing
description: The service supports content chosen for partial attention, multitasking, or ambient entertainment rather than focused viewing.
aliases: background viewing| multitasking content| ambient viewing| passive watching| second-screen viewing
examples: I put on a comedy special while doing something else.  The content worked well without constant attention.  I found a suitable background show quickly.

name: Comfort Viewing
description: The service makes familiar, reassuring, or frequently rewatched content easy to access and continue.
aliases: comfort viewing| familiar shows| rewatching| favorite content| easy fallback
examples: I returned to a familiar series without searching.  A comfort show was an easy fallback when nothing new appealed to me.  The recently watched row supported my usual routine.

name: Familiar-Content Access
description: Previously watched, known, or intentionally sought content is easy to locate without requiring broad exploration.
aliases: familiar-content access| known titles| previously watched| recent content| return to show
examples: I found the show I already knew from a visible row.  Locating a familiar title took longer than expected.  I could return to my usual series without exploring unfamiliar content.

name: Deliberate Content Discovery
description: The service supports careful discovery through descriptions, categories, search, and comparison when users want to make an informed choice.
aliases: deliberate content discovery| careful browsing| informed selection| compare titles| planned discovery
examples: I compared descriptions before choosing a film.  The available information helped me make a considered decision.  I found worthwhile content after a deliberate search.

name: Category Clarity
description: Content categories and row labels are distinct, understandable, and precise enough to help users narrow their choices.
aliases: category clarity| category precision| row labels| genre categories| content classification
examples: The category label accurately described the titles.  Several rows seemed to overlap without a clear difference.  A precise category helped me narrow the search.

name: Casual Browsing
description: The service supports low-effort exploration across rows and previews when users are open to options but have no fixed target.
aliases: casual browsing| relaxed browsing| row exploration| browsing without a target| informal discovery
examples: I scrolled through a few rows without a specific title in mind.  Casual browsing led me to something entertaining.  I stopped browsing when the options became repetitive.
